evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Addressed to the fieldworker about the visit, this records whether the survey team was proactively contacted by community or party actors around access, not the respondent's own partisanship; the actor is external to the respondent.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: The subject of the feeling is the interviewer within this one interview, so a positive answer expresses felt intimidation during the encounter and need not imply any bodily act or respondent-side fear.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: This narrows threat to bodily intimidation in the same encounter, so it is a distinct act from felt threat; a felt-danger report need not coincide with a physical-threat report.

evidence.quote: honest, in between, or misleading?

claims.text: Candour is a three-valued global attribution of respondent demeanour made by the interviewer after the encounter; it is an evaluated impression, not a verified count of truthful answers.

evidence.quote: must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: A forced choice opposing presidential exemption from law and courts against obligatory obedience yields an abstract constitutional stance, not a verdict on any named ruling or officeholder.

evidence.quote: armed forces should never intervene

claims.text: This states a general norm against military entry into politics, paired with a conditional legitimation of takeover amid abuse; it is a principle-level stance, not a judgment about a specific coup.

evidence.quote: Who should be responsible for

claims.text: Oversight of MPs is posed as a normative allocation among president or executive, parliament or council, party, voters and no one, recording who ought to be accountable rather than any actual oversight act.

evidence.quote: the [president] does [his] job?

claims.text: The presidential counterpart reuses the same fixed option set as the MP item, so an office-to-office difference is measurable only within those offered categories and carries no open-ended other.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: The respondent rates the likelihood of community harassment of a hypothetical woman candidate, an anticipated social reaction that does not report harassment actually witnessed or experienced.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more

claims.text: The item requests a desired direction and amount of state effort relative to current action; assenting to more effort is an evaluative demand, not evidence that present effort is deficient in fact.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address

claims.text: The stem frames a single top-priority pick among listed rights concerns, so the field records a capped choice and cannot be read as independent salience or support for each concern separately.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Justification is conditional on a declared health emergency and about a possible measure, so agreement endorses a hypothetical policing power rather than describing enforcement that occurred.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Records the respondent's belief about survey sponsorship across distinct options such as party, government, research company and a divine source; misattribution is possible and the field is not an audit of the actual commissioning body.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Stated willingness to be recontacted carries a separate not-applicable category for respondents lacking a mobile number, so the field is not a plain refusal-versus-consent dichotomy across all respondents.

inquiries.alternatives: If felt threat without physical threat co-occurs with a misleading candour judgment, threat reads as relational unease shaping credibility assessment; if felt threat is confined to physical-threat encounters, the two threat items collapse into one safety indicator and demeanour stands apart; a pattern in which only physical threat tracks distrust supports an incident-based reading over dispositional suspicion.
inquiries.ceiling: Interviewer-administered fields with no interviewer identifier among the selected items, so interviewer composition and clustering cannot be separated from encounter variation; no respondent-side threat measure and no verification of true candour; nominal-only association, no causal or distributional conclusion.
inquiries.question: Does felt threat during the interview track bodily threat and low assessed candour within the same encounters, or do interviewer-side experiential, bodily and demeanour reports diverge?
